exact_source_excerpt: Union Alpha wishes to be ox Alpha
exact_output_excerpt: 联合阿尔法希望成为牛阿尔法
explanation: In this construction, ‘Union Alpha’ and ‘ox Alpha’ function as contrasted names/labels. Rendering both as ordinary Chinese descriptions loses the supplied Latin-label identities and makes the contrast no longer reliably recoverable. I would treat this as material entity identity loss, not merely harmless terminology localization.

exact_source_excerpt: 目標設定しないと止まってしまう
exact_output_excerpt: If I don't set a goal, I'll stop
explanation: Japanese omits the subject. In the local first-person context (‘I’m re-experimenting’), the English first-person reading is natural, but the source can also leave open that the work/experiment stops. The supplied source does not establish a unique subject, so this is not a confirmed material error.

exact_output_excerpt: “China must be ahead” Trump dismisses AI speed-control debate
explanation: Korean ‘중국 앞서야’ means that the implicit actor must get ahead of/outpace China. It does not say that China must be ahead. The English reverses the headline’s competitive direction and is a material meaning error.

exact_output_excerpt: “必须领先中国” 特朗普否认定调AI减速论
explanation: ‘必须领先中国’ supports the Korean direction: the implicit actor must lead/outpace China. This direction is faithful; the headline’s ellipsis does not require naming the implicit actor.
